title: Getting started with xEdit (FO4Edit): loading plugins and reading the window
content:
Getting started with xEdit (FO4Edit): loading plugins and reading the window
xEdit for Fallout 4 is FO4Edit.exe. Run it from anywhere except the game's Data folder; it finds Data through the registry (or -D:<path>). With Mod Organizer 2, add it as an executable and start it from MO2 so it sees your mods. On start you pick which plugins to load: double-click one plugin to load just it and its masters; right-click > Select None to clear; hold Shift while confirming to skip building reference info (faster, but Referenced By stays empty). xEdit cannot change the load order - change it in your mod manager and restart xEdit. Left side: the navigation tree (every plugin in load order, every record). Right side: the View tab shows every version of the selected record side by side - leftmost column is the master, rightmost is the winner, the version the game uses. Referenced By lists every record that uses the selected one (double-click to jump). Messages is the log (load errors, results of every command). Information has the built-in help; the Legend button explains the colours. Changes are saved when you close xEdit (or Save in the main menu): a dialog lists every changed file - untick any file that is not yours. xEdit keeps backups in Data\FO4Edit Backups (plugin.esp.backup.<date>) and reference caches in Data\FO4Edit Cache.

title: Finding which mods conflict with each other in xEdit (FO4Edit): conflicts vs overrides, colours and filters
content:
Finding which mods conflict with each other in xEdit (FO4Edit): conflicts vs overrides, colours and filters
An override is a plugin changing a record from a master - normal and harmless on its own. A conflict needs at least three versions of the same record (master + two overrides) where the overrides change different things: the last plugin in the load order wins and the other plugin's changes are lost (conflict loser). Conflict detection compares the parsed field data, not just that two plugins touch the same record. To see them: right-click the left tree > Apply Filter to show Conflicts (or start xEdit with -VeryQuickShowConflicts / -vqsc). Colours are explained by the Legend button (top right); in short a conflict loser shows red, an override with no conflict green/yellow, and a field identical to the master greyed - an ITM (Identical To Master) dirty edit. In the View tab, right-click > Hide no conflict and empty rows to see only what differs. Four ways to handle a conflict: do nothing if it does not matter, change the load order, make a patch plugin, or drop one of the mods.

title: Making a compatibility patch in xEdit by hand (Copy as override, drag and drop)
content:
Making a compatibility patch in xEdit by hand (Copy as override, drag and drop)
Load the conflicting plugins, apply the conflict filter, select a conflicting record, right-click it > Copy as override into... > tick <new file> and name the patch (or pick your existing patch). xEdit adds the needed masters. The patch is now the rightmost column (the winner). Then bring over what each mod should keep: drag a value from another plugin's column and drop it on your patch's column (drag whole list entries from their top row), or right-click a field > Edit (or F2 / double-click) to type a value. Repeat for every conflicting record, then save. Copy as override only copies the record itself; Deep copy as override also copies its child records (for example a cell's references). Only ever edit your own plugins or new patch files. The automatic 'Create Merged Patch' (Other menu) is obsolete and unsupported according to the xEdit team - it only merges a few record types.

title: Cleaning a plugin with Quick Auto Clean (QAC): how and why one plugin at a time
content:
Cleaning a plugin with Quick Auto Clean (QAC): how and why one plugin at a time
Use FO4EditQuickAutoClean.exe (shipped with xEdit), or start FO4Edit with -quickautoclean (-qac); add it as a separate executable in MO2. Pick ONE plugin (double-click it). QAC removes ITM records, undeletes and disables deleted references (moved to Z -30000, the same effect as deleting without the crash risk), runs three times and saves between passes; then close xEdit. -quickclean cleans twice and asks before saving. Clean only one plugin at a time with nothing else loaded but its masters: with other mods loaded, a record identical to its master can count as a conflict winner and is no longer removed. There are no intentional ITMs according to the xEdit author. The old manual commands (Apply Filter for Cleaning, Remove Identical to Master, Undelete and Disable References) are deprecated - QAC replaces them. Deleted NAVMESHES cannot be fixed automatically (xEdit's own 'Undelete navmeshes' script is marked work in progress, Fallout 3/New Vegas only, not for real plugins): they need manual repair. Wild edits (changes the author did not mean) also need a human. Mod authors should clean their own mods before release.

title: Check for Errors, circular leveled lists, and Add / Sort / Clean Masters in xEdit
content:
Check for Errors, circular leveled lists, and Add / Sort / Clean Masters in xEdit
Right-click a plugin > Check for Errors reports anything that does not match xEdit's record definitions; results go to Messages. Most serious: 'Could not be resolved' (an unresolved reference - the record points at something missing from the plugin and its masters) - the mod author must fix those. The official DLC have known errors: do not try to fix them. Check for Circular Leveled Lists finds leveled lists that end up containing themselves (the game can loop and crash). Add Masters adds master files AND renumbers the plugin's own records so they keep pointing at the right file - never type a new master into the header by hand, or your own records turn into overrides of the new master. Sort Masters puts the master list in load order (safe when the masters are only DLC or one ESP; look closer when several ESPs are masters, their order can matter). Clean Masters removes masters the plugin no longer uses (a master still in use stays; the bundled script 'List records referencing specific plugin' shows why). Do not strip masters from other people's mods.

title: FormIDs in xEdit, Change FormID, Renumber, Compact FormIDs for ESL and its dangers
content:
FormIDs in xEdit, Change FormID, Renumber, Compact FormIDs for ESL and its dangers
xEdit shows load-order-corrected FormIDs: the first two hex digits are the plugin's load-order slot (or FE:xxx for a light plugin), the rest is the record's own ID. Inside the file the prefix is the index in its master list. F2 on a record (Change FormID) gives it a new FormID; Change Referencing Records re-points everything that used one record to another; Renumber FormIDs from... renumbers all of a plugin's own records. ESL: set the ESL flag in File Header > Record Flags (Edit). New records must fit the light range; Compact FormIDs for ESL renumbers them to fit. Dangers of compacting (official docs): it changes FormIDs, which is like uninstalling the mod for existing saves; patches and plugins that use it as a master break; Papyrus GetFormFromFile with old IDs breaks; new NPCs need FaceGen regenerated in the CK and custom voice files renamed (their names contain the FormID); avoid compacting INFO and NPC_ records. Safe: compact BEFORE release. Start xEdit with -PseudoESL to see which plugins could be light without changes (shown with an FE:xxx number). A new plugin made in xEdit 4.1.5f (header 1.0) numbers its new records from 001 (tested).

title: Merging plugins, ESP to ESM, splitting into ESM + ESP, and comparing two versions in xEdit
content:
Merging plugins, ESP to ESM, splitting into ESM + ESP, and comparing two versions in xEdit
Merge: load order must have the receiving plugin BELOW the ones being merged into it. Select all record groups of the plugin to merge > right-click > Deep copy as override into... > pick the receiver (accept adding masters), check Messages for errors, save. ESP to ESM: load it alone, File Header > Record Flags > Edit > tick ESM, save, rename the extension; doing this in xEdit also writes the ONAM list the game needs for overrides of master records - simply renaming the file does not. Split into a pair: copy the ESP to an ESM file, set the ESM flag in the copy, then in the ESP add the ESM to the master list - all records in the ESP become overrides of the ESM. Compare two versions: load one, mark its masters Hidden, right-click > Compare to... and open the other file (it loads read-only), then Apply Filter with 'by conflict status' + Identical to Master + Override without Conflict + Conflict status inherited by Parent; drag records from the read-only version into yours if needed. 'Create delta patch using...' copies only the records that changed between the versions.

title: ModGroups and "Only Master and Leafs" in xEdit: hiding conflicts you have already checked
content:
ModGroups and "Only Master and Leafs" in xEdit: hiding conflicts you have already checked
A ModGroup says: in these plugins, the later ones already contain everything the earlier ones change, so hide the older versions. It does not merge or change any file; hidden versions just stop taking part in conflict detection. A ModGroup is only offered when at least two of its plugins are active and their load order matches. Files: <EXE name>.modgroups next to the EXE, or <plugin name>.modgroups in Data (keep it with the mod). Line prefixes: + optional, - neither target nor source, @ not a source, # not a target, ! forbidden (if active the group is invalid), } ignore load order, { ignore load order inside a block; file.esp:CRC32 limits the group to that exact file version. Create/Edit ModGroup are in the right-click menu. 'Only Master and Leafs' (View tab menu) is similar: it shows only the master and the plugins nothing else builds on - only safe if those authors did their patches right.

title: FO4Edit command-line switches (xEdit 4.1.5f) and the trailing-backslash rule
content:
FO4Edit command-line switches (xEdit 4.1.5f) and the trailing-backslash rule
Modes: -fo4 (game), -edit, -view, -quickautoclean/-qac, -quickclean/-qc, -VeryQuickShowConflicts/-vqsc, -quickshowconflicts/-qsc, -setesm/-clearesm, -autogamelink/-agl, -script:<file.pas> (run a script after loading), -autoload (skip plugin selection, load plugins.txt), -autoexit (close when the mode finishes), -quickedit:<plugin> (preselect one plugin and its masters), -moprofile:<name>, -IgnoreESL, -PseudoESL, -DontCache / -DontCacheLoad / -DontCacheSave, -AllowDirectSaves[:files], -cp:<codepage>, -l:<language>. Paths: -D:<Data> -P:<plugins.txt> -C:<cache> -S:<scripts> -T:<temp> -B:<backups> -O:<LOD output> -I:<ini> -G:<saves> -R:<log file>. Folder paths must end with a backslash - and do NOT wrap such a path in quotes, because \" makes Windows treat the quote as part of the text and the path breaks (seen on our test bench: xEdit then sat waiting). Use a folder without spaces or a short path. In MO2 put switches in the executable's Arguments box.

title: How an xEdit script runs: Initialize, Process and Finalize
content:
How an xEdit script runs: Initialize, Process and Finalize
An xEdit script is a Pascal file (.pas) in the Edit Scripts folder starting with 'unit userscript;' and ending with 'end.'. Run it with right-click > Apply Script... (also from the Referenced By tab). xEdit calls three optional functions, all returning an integer: Initialize once at the start; Process(e: IInterface) once for every record under what you selected - select a plugin and it runs for every record in it, walked from the last child back to the first; Finalize once at the end. Return 0 to continue. A non-zero result from Initialize stops the script (Process and Finalize are skipped); a non-zero result from Process stops the record loop but Finalize STILL runs. If Process does not exist the record loop is skipped entirely - so a script that only needs a few groups can do all its work in Initialize, which is much faster (Fallout4.esm alone has 1,549,276 records). By default Process only receives main records; the global ScriptProcessElements changes that. Write 'Mode: Silent' in the script's header comment to suppress messages. Errors are reported in Messages as 'Exception in <unit> line N: ...'. New scripts start from _newscript_.pas in Edit Scripts.

title: xEdit script language (JvInterpreter Pascal): what works and what does not (tested)
content:
xEdit script language (JvInterpreter Pascal): what works and what does not (tested)
Tested working in FO4Edit 4.1.5f: const; global var shared between Initialize/Process/Finalize; your own functions and procedures, var parameters; for..to/downto, while, repeat..until, Break, Continue, Exit, case..of..else; div, mod, Inc; and/or/not; Round, Trunc, FloatToStr, IntToStr, IntToHex, StrToInt (also '$FF' hex), StrToIntDef, Pos, Copy, Length, LowerCase, UpperCase, Trim, SameText, StringReplace with [rfReplaceAll, rfIgnoreCase], Format('%s %d %.2f', [...]); TStringList (Create, Add, Sort, IndexOf, Count, CommaText, Values[], SaveToFile, Free); try..finally; try..except on E: Exception do ... E.Message. NOT available: BoolToStr ('Undeclared Identifier') - write your own small function. Always Free what you Create (TStringList) in a finally block. Script files must be valid for xEdit's interpreter, not just Delphi: test-run every script on a copy of your files.

title: xEdit script functions for finding and reading records (tested names and arguments)
content:
xEdit script functions for finding and reading records (tested names and arguments)
Files: FileCount, FileByIndex(i), FileByName('Fallout4.esm'), GetFileName(f), RecordCount(f), RecordByIndex(f, i), MasterCount(f), MasterByIndex(f, i). Records: GroupBySignature(f, 'WEAP') then ElementCount/ElementByIndex; MainRecordByEditorID(GroupBySignature(f, 'WEAP'), '10mm'); RecordByHexFormID('00004822') (load-order FormID as text). Look records up by Editor ID rather than a remembered FormID - on our bench 0004822B turned out to be a placed picture frame, the 10mm pistol is 00004822. Fields: GetElementEditValues(r, 'FULL'), GetElementEditValues(r, 'DNAM\Damage - Base'), GetElementNativeValues for numbers, ElementBySignature(r, 'KWDA'), ElementByName(r, 'Leveled List Entries'), ElementByPath, GetEditValue(element), LinksTo(element) (the record a FormID field points at). Identity: Name(r) ('10mm "10mm" [WEAP:00004822]'), EditorID, Signature, FormID (file-specific) vs GetLoadOrderFormID, FullPath/PathName. Overrides: MasterOrSelf, OverrideCount, WinningOverride, IsWinningOverride, HighestOverrideOrSelf(record, maxLoadOrder) - two arguments. Usage: ReferencedByCount / ReferencedByIndex (needs references built, i.e. do not skip with Shift). Output: AddMessage(text).

title: xEdit script functions for creating and changing records (tested)
content:
xEdit script functions for creating and changing records (tested)
New plugin: m := AddNewFileName('MyMod.esp'); SetIsESL(m, True) for a light plugin; AddMasterIfMissing(m, 'Fallout4.esm'). Before copying a record into it: AddRequiredElementMasters(rec, m, asNew) - adds whatever masters the record needs. Copy: wbCopyElementToFile(rec, m, True, True) = copy AS A NEW record (new FormID in your plugin); wbCopyElementToFile(rec, m, False, True) = copy as an OVERRIDE of the original. Copying a placed reference (REFR) adds the override of its cell automatically. New record from scratch: g := Add(m, 'KYWD', True) creates the top group, then r := Add(g, 'KYWD', True). Editor ID: SetEditorID(r, 'MyMod_Name') - two arguments. Set fields: SetElementEditValues(r, 'FULL', 'My Name'), SetElementNativeValues for numbers; a FormID field takes the 8-digit load-order FormID as text, e.g. IntToHex(GetLoadOrderFormID(target), 8). Add a list entry: e := ElementAssign(list, HighInteger, nil, False) then set its fields - counts like KSIZ (keywords) and LLCT (leveled list entries) update by themselves. Remove(element) deletes. Changes are saved when xEdit closes.

title: xEdit's bundled xEditAPI.pas is incomplete: argument counts and missing functions (4.1.5f)
content:
xEdit's bundled xEditAPI.pas is incomplete: argument counts and missing functions (4.1.5f)
xEditAPI.pas (in Edit Scripts) lists script functions for editing in Delphi, but checked against the functions the 4.1.5f script engine really registers, 7 have the wrong number of arguments: HighestOverrideOrSelf takes 2 (record, max load order), SetEditorID takes 2 (record, new ID), SortKey 2, GroupType 1, UpdateRefs 1, FileWriteToStream 3, NifTextureListResource 3. 22 real functions are missing from it, among them GetIsESL, SetIsESL, CanBeESL, GetMasters, ReferencesCount, ReferencesByIndex, BeginUpdate/EndUpdate, IndexedPath, bscrc32, CreateHashFO4, wbCopyElementToFileWithPrefixAndSuffix. The host also provides globals not in that file: FileByName, RecordByHexFormID, AddNewFile, AddRequiredElementMasters, ClearMessages, ConflictAllForMainRecord / ConflictThisForMainRecord, ApplyFilter / RemoveFilter with Filter* settings, TempPath, wbSelectedFilesToFileNames. Trust a real test run over the declaration file.

title: Running an xEdit script from the command line (-script) saves changes WITHOUT asking
content:
Running an xEdit script from the command line (-script) saves changes WITHOUT asking
FO4Edit -script:MyScript.pas -autoload loads the plugins from plugins.txt, selects every loaded file and applies the script to all of them. Script mode is one of xEdit's automatic modes: when xEdit closes, every changed plugin is saved without the save dialog. So run command-line scripts only on copies: point -D: at a copy of Data, -P: at your own plugins.txt, and -C: -B: -R: at your own folders. A relative script name is looked for in the scripts folder (-S:). In our 4.1.5f test, -autoexit did not close the window after the script; xEdit printed 'You can close this application now', and closing it normally saved the files. Have the script write a small 'done' file in Finalize if you automate this.

title: Building a whole mod as one ESP in xEdit using only vanilla assets
content:
Building a whole mod as one ESP in xEdit using only vanilla assets
If a mod only reuses vanilla meshes, textures, materials and sounds, everything can live in one plugin. In xEdit: right-click a plugin > Create New File... (or pick <new file> in any copy dialog). New things: right-click a vanilla record > Copy as new record into... your plugin - it gets a new FormID in your file and keeps pointing at the vanilla model; then give it its own Editor ID and change name and stats (F2, double-click, or right-click > Edit). Changing vanilla things: Copy as override into... and edit. Getting it into the game: a crafting recipe (COBJ), adding it to a vanilla leveled list (override the LVLI and add an entry), or placing it: Copy as new record of a vanilla placed reference (REFR), then change its base object and position - xEdit adds the cell override for you. Masters are added automatically. Then Check for Errors and test in game. Tested on our bench: new weapon + recipe + leveled-list entry + placed copy in Vault 111 = one 6.5 KB ESP with 0 errors. What still needs files or the Creation Kit: NEW NPCs or changed faces need FaceGen meshes/textures (export in the CK with Ctrl+F4 and ship them, or the face goes dark); voiced dialogue needs voice files; navmesh for new walkable areas is best done in the CK; new Papyrus scripts need compiled .pex files. A record copied as new keeps the vanilla scripts it already had (those scripts ship with the game).

title: Crafting recipe (COBJ) and leveled list (LVLI) fields when making a mod in xEdit
content:
Crafting recipe (COBJ) and leveled list (LVLI) fields when making a mod in xEdit
COBJ (Constructible Object): CNAM - Created Object = the thing made; BNAM - Workbench Keyword = which bench shows it (e.g. WorkbenchChemlab for the chemistry station - set it on purpose, a copied recipe keeps its old bench); FVPA - Components = the materials and counts; FNAM - Category = menu category keywords; Conditions = when it appears (perks, etc.); INTV = data. LVLI (Leveled Item): 'Leveled List Entries', each 'LVLO - Base Data' with Level, Reference and Count; LLCT is the entry count and is updated by xEdit. Adding your item to a vanilla leveled list means overriding that list, which conflicts with any other mod that edits the same list (the last one loaded wins) - check conflicts or use a patch. Example from our bench: the vanilla list LL_10mm_Pistol_RandomTemplate [LVLI:0018DFED] with one entry (the 10mm pistol 00004822) became two entries.

title: xEdit View tab and keyboard shortcuts (editing fields, jumping, lists)
content:
xEdit View tab and keyboard shortcuts (editing fields, jumping, lists)
View tab right-click: Edit, Add, Remove, Clear, Remove from selected records, Copy to selected records (and Copy multiple to selected records - apply one value to many selected records), Move up/down, Sort by this row, Compare referenced records in this row, Clipboard (copy path, full path, indexed path, signature, name), Hide no conflict and empty rows, ModGroups on/off, Only Master and Leafs. Keys: F2 edits the selected field (in the left tree F2 changes the record's FormID); double-click a number or FormID to edit it in place; Shift+double-click a text to edit it in a multi-line editor; Ctrl+click a FormID to jump to that record; Ctrl+Up/Down moves an entry in an unordered list; Ctrl+C copies; Del deletes the selected records in the left tree; Ctrl+1..5 sets a bookmark, Alt+1..5 jumps to it; Ctrl+F3 Assets Browser, Alt+F3 Worldspace Browser; Ctrl+W on a weather record opens the weather editor. In the plugin list: Space ticks, Shift skips building references.
